title: Low-Field J-Coupling Spectroscopy Measured with a Diamond Nitrogen Vacancy Spectrometer
authors: Stephen J. DeVience, John W. Blanchard, Camille G. McDonnell, Ronald L. Walsworth
abstract: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields. NV spin states can be initialized and read out optically with high spatial resolution, enabling detection of pL-scale volumes of nuclear spins. Using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR), standard NMR spectroscopy techniques such as free decay, spin echo, and PGSE have been performed with Hz-scale spectral resolution using NV-diamond sensors. However, using NV detection for conventional high-resolution NMR at multi-tesla fields is challenging due to the need to manipulate NV electronic spins at resonance frequencies 100 GHz or higher. Low-field J-coupling spectroscopy provides an alternative path to chemical resolution in a regime more easily accessible to NVs. Here, we demonstrate homonuclear and heteronuclear J-coupling spectroscopy using an NV-NMR spectrometer based on permanent magnets operating at $\sim$890 kHz proton Larmor frequency (bias magnetic field $\sim$21 mT). This field strength enables chemical characterization based on J-coupling using sequences such as Synchronized Echo (SyncE) and Spin-Echo Double Resonance (SEDOR), which do not require the strong chemical shift dispersion and pristine field homogeneity of high-field NMR. The frequency range is easily detected by NVs using standard XY dynamical decoupling sequences and is well-suited for applying Overhauser DNP, which can boost proton signal by two orders of magnitude. We acquire initial NV-NMR measurements of T$_1$, T$_2$, and Overhauser DNP in glycerol before advancing to SEDOR spectroscopy of methanol-$^{13}$C and a methanol-$^{13}$C/acetonitrile-2-$^{13}$C mixture at sample volumes $\sim$50 pL, in which we demonstrate measurement of $^1J_\text{CH}$ couplings and resolution between species. We also acquire a homonuclear J-coupling spectrum of a natural-abundance propylene carbonate sample.
summary: This paper details the use of Nitrogen Vacancy centers in diamond as a quantum sensor to perform low-field NMR spectroscopy. By focusing on J-coupling rather than chemical shifts, the authors overcome the technical hurdles of high-field NMR for NV detection. The results prove the feasibility of high-resolution chemical characterization in minute sample volumes using this quantum sensing platform.
main_problem: To perform high-resolution Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, specifically J-coupling measurements, on small samples using Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, circumventing the limitations of traditional high-field NMR.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated homonuclear and heteronuclear J-coupling spectroscopy at low magnetic fields using the NV-NMR spectrometer, achieving chemical resolution in small volumes ($\sim 50 	ext{ pL}$).
method: The technique adapts standard NMR pulse sequences (like SEDOR and SyncE) for detection via the NV electronic spin state using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR) at low bias fields ($\sim 21 	ext{ mT}$).
model_or_system: The physical platform is an NV-center in diamond acting as a quantum sensor for nuclear spins. The system operates by coupling the nuclear spin dynamics (NMR) to the measurable electronic spin state of the NV center.
key_observables: J-coupling constants ($^1J_{	ext{CH}}$), $T_1$ and $T_2$ relaxation times, and Overhauser DNP enhancement factors.
important_parameters: Low magnetic field ($\sim 21 	ext{ mT}$), spectral resolution in the kHz range, and small sample volumes ($\sim 50 	ext{ pL}$).
main_assumptions: The technique assumes that the NV electronic spin can coherently read out the nuclear spin evolution via CASR, bypassing the need for high microwave frequencies required at multi-tesla fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectrometer setup, time-domain measurements (free-decay, spin-echo, DNP), and spectral results showing J-coupling dips for various molecules.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for a low-field approach to demonstrating initial measurements on simple liquids (glycerol), followed by complex measurements of heteronuclear and homonuclear J-couplings in model organic molecules.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum sensing (NV centers) with fundamental chemical physics (NMR spectroscopy), demonstrating a pathway to miniaturize and simplify high-resolution spectroscopy for quantum applications.

Detection of NMR signals from liquid in the sample tube is performed by the adjacent NV-diamond sensor via CASR NMR measurements. Pulses are first applied with orthogonal 1H and 13C coils to induce NMR signals from the liquid sample, held adjacent to the NV-NMR sensor. CASR NMR measurements are performed by the NVs, in which the NV electronic spins are initialized and read out with 532 nm laser pulses and manipulated by microwave (MW) pulses from the MW loop. Each measurement consists of two blocks of NV spin-state optical initialization, an NV DD pulse sequence controlled by microwaves, and NV photoluminescence (PL) readout.
